author: Claude, 9 Nov 2026
status: frozen BEFORE any new inference on these crops
question: Do large crop margins (writing small after resizing to 64 px) contribute to errors, especially deletions, on unfamiliar writers?
crops: all 160 JH/DS new-writer crops; Jy excluded (294/298 already tight, and ink detection missed light first strokes, so tightening would cut letters)
box_rule: sensitive ink mask (median-background difference > max(10, 0.2*p99.5)), components >= max(6, 5e-5*area) px; box = ink box padded by max(6, 0.35*ink height) vertically and max(10, 0.8*ink height) horizontally; border-touching components dropped for JH19.1/JH22.1/JH26.1/JH5.1 (corner shading). Every changed box was visually checked to keep all target strokes.
groups: dose = kept height fraction (box height / crop height): large margin <= 0.6; control >= 0.85; middle in between; 4 flagged crops reported separately
reader: exported S1 seed-1 model (results_strategies_s0s3/results/models/PP-OCRv5_server_rec_board2notes_S1), Mac CPU static reader, same code for both arms; originals re-scored with the same reader
metric: mean line CER (lower-case, spaces normalised), Levenshtein substitutions/deletions/insertions, crops better/worse
supported_if: ALL of: (1) large-margin group: mean CER change (tight - original) has photo-cluster bootstrap 95% CI below 0; (2) large-margin deletions decrease; (3) large-margin change minus control change has 95% CI below 0. Otherwise: not supported.
caveats: manual/oracle boxes, not an app feature; JH/DS already informed development; one reader; CPU scorer
inputs: original arm reads the untouched source files; tight arm reads lossless PNG crops of the same decoded pixels
